sections.heading: Discover Downtown Concord
sections.html: Downtown Concord is the vibrant historic heart of Concord, North Carolina. Located just 25 minutes from Charlotte (see commute details), this charming neighborhood combines rich history dating back to the 18th century with modern amenities and a thriving arts scene. Tree-lined streets, locally-owned boutiques, award-winning restaurants, and beautifully preserved architecture make Downtown Concord one of the most desirable places to live in Cabarrus County.

sections.heading: Community & Character
sections.html:
Downtown Concord is the historic heart of Cabarrus County — a walkable core centered on Union Street, with the landmark Cabarrus County Courthouse, locally owned shops and restaurants, and a steady calendar of street festivals, parades, and community events. The residential streets around downtown mix historic homes with newer infill, drawing a blend of long-time residents, young professionals, and families who want to be steps from downtown life.

Major revitalization investment — including the streetscape work along Union Street and the redevelopment of the former Cannon Mills Plant 1 site at Gibson Mill — has brought new dining, retail, and gathering spaces downtown in recent years, while the historic architecture and small-town feel remain intact. For current population and income figures, the U.S. Census Bureau's American Community Survey data for Concord is the authoritative source.

sections.heading: Housing Market Overview
sections.html:
Home Types Downtown

Diverse housing options — from historic homes on tree-lined streets near Union Street to modern condos and townhomes — make downtown one of Concord's most varied areas. Most downtown addresses fall in the 28025 ZIP code; see our 28027 vs 28025 comparison on the blog for how the two sides of Concord differ.

Market Picture

Downtown-specific figures move with a small number of sales, so the reliable benchmark is the citywide data on our market reports page (Canopy MLS; May 2026: median sale price $360,000, 43 days on market for Concord overall). Historic homes in good condition tend to command a premium for their character and walkability, and renovated properties near Union Street draw strong interest. Contact Franklin at (704) 904-5142 for current downtown listings and recent sales on your street.

Shopping & Services

Parks & Recreation

🌳 McGill Rose Garden

Beautiful historic garden with over 200 rose varieties, perfect for evening strolls

⛲ Union Street Park

Downtown green space with playground, splash pad, and event pavilion

sections.heading: Top Attractions & Things to Do
sections.html:
Historic Courthouse

Beautiful 1876 courthouse, now a museum showcasing Cabarrus County history and architecture

Cabarrus Arena & Events Center

Concert venue and event space hosting national acts, sports events, and community gatherings

Arts District

Monthly art walks, galleries, public art installations, and the Cabarrus Arts Council gallery

Charlotte Motor Speedway

World-famous NASCAR track just 10 minutes away, hosting major races and events year-round

Culinary Scene

Over 50 restaurants from farm-to-table to international cuisine, plus craft breweries

Annual Events

Christmas parade, summer concert series, First Friday celebrations, and seasonal festivals

sections.heading: Why Choose Downtown Concord?
sections.html:
Perfect Location

Downtown Concord offers the ideal balance: small-town charm with big-city access. Just 25 minutes from Charlotte's vibrant urban core, residents enjoy the best of both worlds. Learn more about our proximity to Charlotte →

Community Spirit

Known for its welcoming atmosphere and tight-knit community, Downtown Concord hosts year-round events that bring neighbors together and create lasting connections. Discover area lifestyle →

Strong Appreciation

With steady home value growth and increasing demand, Downtown Concord represents an excellent investment opportunity in an established, historic neighborhood.

Walkable Lifestyle

Leave the car at home and stroll to restaurants, shops, parks, and entertainment. Downtown Concord's walkability is a key feature that residents love.
